andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh notifies mayoral reservation roster for 17 municipal corporations
facts: The state notified reservation categories for mayoral offices in 17 municipal corporations ahead of civic elections.
Five mayoral posts are reserved for BCs, two for SCs, one for STs, five for women under the general category; four are unreserved.
Visakhapatnam, Guntur, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Kadapa are in the general-women category; Vijayawada and Tirupati are unreserved.
Mangalagiri-Tadepalli is the sole ST-reserved corporation; the Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department issued the orders under the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act, 1994.
The reservation roster was to be forwarded to the State Election Commission; the notification is a preparatory step, not an election schedule.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: Andhra Pradesh’s BC local-body reservation process and commission recommendations were covered. Today: the state notified the mayoral reservation roster for all 17 municipal corporations, advancing preparations for civic elections. The roster allocates posts across BC, SC, ST, women and unreserved categories.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Urban local self-government; constitutional framework for reservation and representation in local bodies.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the 17-corporation total and the mayoral roster distribution: BC 5, SC 2, ST 1, general women 5 and unreserved 4.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how transparent reservation rosters can improve representation in urban local government while ensuring compliance with statutory and constitutional rules.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct Andhra Pradesh link: the roster covers all 17 state municipal corporations, including Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Guntur and Mangalagiri-Tadepalli.

andhraPradesh.headline: Drought leaves most of Prakasam’s normal kharif area unsown
facts: A report on Prakasam district said crops had been raised on 8,642 hectares against a normal kharif sowing area of 55,774 hectares, or about 15.46% of the target.
The reported figures imply that roughly 85% of the normal kharif area remained unsown at the time of reporting.
Drought assessment cited 18 mandals in Prakasam as severely affected and 10 as moderately affected.
The report identified rain-fed red gram among the crops facing serious stress; final crop-loss assessment was still pending.
The reported stress extends to farm livelihoods, agricultural labour and water availability.
andhraPradesh.summary: A Times of India report published on 12 October described sharply curtailed kharif cultivation in Prakasam amid drought. It reported low sown area and drought classifications across 28 mandals; final crop-loss assessment had not yet been completed.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Drought vulnerability, rain-fed agriculture, groundwater and irrigation dependence, and rural livelihoods.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Prakasam’s reported normal kharif sowing area was 55,774 hectares; 8,642 hectares were reported sown, and 28 mandals were classified as severely or moderately affected.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how rainfall deficits can affect agricultural output, rural employment and water security, and evaluate the role of timely crop assessment and drought response.

andhraPradesh.headline: ₹3,222 crore development works launched for Tirupati and Tirumala
facts: The Chief Minister virtually launched development works reported to be worth ₹3,222 crore for Tirupati and Tirumala.
A proposed Integrated Pilgrim Township near Alipiri–SV Zoo Park Road accounts for ₹2,750 crore and is planned with 2,700 rooms, a transport terminal and parking facilities.
₹230 crore was sanctioned for infrastructure for a 418-acre TTD employee housing layout near Vadamalpeta.
Tirupati Urban Development Authority and TTD are to jointly invest ₹242 crore in nine master-plan roads spanning 20 km.
The launch marks the start of project implementation; the announced facilities and works are not reported as completed.

andhraPradesh.headline: Palnadu district issues ward-reservation gazettes for seven urban local bodies
facts: Palnadu district administration published ward-reservation gazette notices dated 13 October 2026 for seven urban local bodies.
The notices cover Sattenapalle, Macherla, Piduguralla, Chilakaluripet and Vinukonda municipalities, and Gurazala and Dachepalli Nagar Panchayats.
The Macherla gazette concerns its second ordinary municipal election and declares wards reserved for ST, SC, BC and women categories.
The Macherla notification cites the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 and the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities reservation rules.
These are ward-level reservation notifications; they do not themselves announce polling dates.
andhraPradesh.summary: Palnadu district’s official portal listed ward-reservation gazettes for seven urban local bodies on 13 October. The notices set category-wise ward arrangements for the next stage of municipal election preparations; the Macherla gazette specifically identifies the statutory basis and reservation categories.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Municipal governance, ward representation and statutory reservation in urban local bodies.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The seven Palnadu urban local bodies named in the notices are Sattenapalle, Macherla, Piduguralla, Chilakaluripet, Vinukonda, Gurazala and Dachepalli.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Explain how ward delimitation and reservation notifications operationalise representation in urban local bodies, and why electoral preparation must distinguish reservation orders from election schedules.

andhraPradesh.headline: National SARAS Mela begins in Vijayawada; formal inauguration scheduled for 15 October
facts: The National SARAS Mela began on 13 October at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada, and is scheduled to run through 31 October.
The Ministry of Rural Development and Andhra Pradesh’s Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty are organising the event.
The official announcement said more than 1,500 women entrepreneurs from Self-Help Groups across 30-plus States and Union Territories are expected to participate.
The mela provides a marketplace for SHG women to sell products directly and connect to wider markets, including through the eSARAS platform.
The President of India is scheduled to formally inaugurate the mela on 15 October; the opening on 13 October is distinct from that planned inauguration.
PIB described this as the first National SARAS Mela held outside the Delhi-NCR region.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: the Vijayawada mela was announced and scheduled. Today: it began at Punnami Ghat, with its run set through 31 October; the formal inauguration remains scheduled for 15 October. It links SHG enterprises with direct sales and broader market access.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: DAY-NRLM, women’s self-help groups, rural livelihoods and market linkage.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The Vijayawada event runs 13–31 October 2026; it is organised with AP’s SERP and the formal inauguration is scheduled for 15 October.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how fairs and digital platforms can help SHG enterprises move from skills and production to market access and sustainable income.

andhraPradesh.headline: APPSC publishes detailed recruitment notifications for five state-service posts
facts: APPSC published detailed recruitment notifications dated 13 October 2026 for five posts or services.
The notifications cover Assistant Director in the A.P. Economics and Statistical Service and Inspector of Factories in the A.P. Factories Service.

Other notified posts are Analyst Grade-II in the A.P. Pollution Control Board, English and Telugu Reporters in A.P. Legislature Services, and Assistant Statistical Officer in the A.P. Economics and Statistical Subordinate Service.
The Commission also listed an addendum to notifications 07/2026, 08/2026 and 19/2026 on its portal on 13 October.
The portal publication confirms the notifications’ release; applicants should consult each detailed notice for eligibility, vacancies and application timelines.

national.headline: First BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting adopts Delhi Declaration
facts: India hosted the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi on 13 October 2026.
BIMSTEC’s seven member states participated: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
The meeting adopted the Delhi Declaration on regional security cooperation.
The declaration calls for cooperation against terrorism, terror financing, radicalisation, organised crime, human trafficking, drug trafficking and cybercrime.
It calls for implementation of BIMSTEC’s convention on combating international terrorism, transnational organised crime and illicit drug trafficking, in force since March 2021.
The meeting also advanced cooperation on information-sharing, mutual legal assistance, extradition and disaster preparedness.
national.summary: India hosted the grouping’s inaugural Home Ministers’ Meeting on 13 October, which concluded with the adoption of the Delhi Declaration. The declaration sets out areas for practical regional security cooperation, including counterterrorism, transnational crime and disaster preparedness.
national.staticLink: BIMSTEC: regional cooperation, institutional architecture and India’s neighbourhood diplomacy
national.prelimsTakeaway: BIMSTEC has seven members; the first Home Ministers’ Meeting was held in New Delhi and adopted the Delhi Declaration.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how regional security cooperation through BIMSTEC can address cross-border threats while strengthening institutional capacity and mutual trust.

national.headline: PM GatiShakti marks five years with expanded national infrastructure-planning platform
facts: The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan was launched in October 2021; its fifth anniversary was marked on 13 October 2026.
Its indigenous geospatial digital platform was developed by BISAG-N.
The platform integrates more than 1,800 data layers covering 58 Central Ministries and Departments and all 36 States and Union Territories.
The Network Planning Group has evaluated more than 400 infrastructure projects worth about ₹20.23 lakh crore under PM GatiShakti principles.
The platform supports coordinated, multimodal and last-mile infrastructure planning; the government said its use is expanding to district-level and social-sector planning.
national.summary: The government marked five years of PM GatiShakti on 13 October and reported the platform’s expanded data coverage and project-planning role. The plan uses integrated geospatial information to support coordinated infrastructure decisions across ministries and states.
national.staticLink: Infrastructure planning, multimodal connectivity and Centre–State coordination
national.prelimsTakeaway: PM GatiShakti is the National Master Plan for multimodal infrastructure connectivity; BISAG-N developed its geospatial platform.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how integrated geospatial planning can reduce infrastructure gaps and coordination failures, while identifying requirements for transparent and inclusive implementation.

national.headline: RINL land e-auction generates ₹366.33 crore in successful bids on Day 1
facts: The National Land Monetization Corporation conducted the first day of an e-auction of land parcels belonging to Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL).
RINL operates Visakhapatnam Steel Plant in Andhra Pradesh.
A total of 150 plots were sold in the first phase, generating successful bids of ₹366.33 crore against an aggregate reserve price of ₹312.48 crore.
The highest auction price exceeded ₹1.80 lakh per square yard.
The second phase, covering the remaining 216 plots, was rescheduled for 30 October 2026.

national.headline: TRAI report records 111.417 crore internet subscribers at end-June 2026
facts: TRAI’s Indian Telecom Services Performance Indicators report for April–June 2026 was published on 12 October 2026.
India had 1,114.17 million internet subscribers at the end of June 2026, up from 1,092.79 million at the end of March.
Of the June total, 1,066.43 million were wireless internet subscribers and 47.73 million were wired subscribers.
Broadband subscribers reached 1,087.50 million; narrowband subscribers declined 0.89% during the quarter.
Total telephone subscribers rose to 1,348.08 million and overall tele-density to 94.31%, from 93.26% at end-March 2026.
national.summary: TRAI’s quarterly performance report, published on 12 October, recorded growth in internet subscriptions and tele-density by the end of June 2026. The figures distinguish wired and wireless access and show continued expansion in broadband subscriptions.

national.headline: President appoints or transfers Governors in six States
facts: A Presidential press communique dated 12 October 2026 announced six Governor appointments or transfers; they take effect when the appointees assume charge.
Om Prakash Mathur was appointed Governor of Keralam, and Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar was appointed Governor of Tamil Nadu.
Braj Mohan Ram was appointed Governor of Odisha; Sudha Yadav, Governor of Karnataka; Dhal Singh Bisen, Governor of Uttarakhand; and Dushyant Gautam, Governor of Sikkim.
The appointments are made by the President under Article 155 of the Constitution.
national.summary: The President announced appointments or transfers affecting the Governorships of six States on 12 October. The communique states that the changes take effect from the dates the appointees assume charge.
national.staticLink: Constitutional office of the Governor: appointment, tenure and role in State government
national.prelimsTakeaway: Article 155 provides that the Governor of a State is appointed by the President by warrant under the President’s hand and seal.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the constitutional role of Governors and how appointment practices relate to federalism and the impartial functioning of State institutions.

facts: The Ministry of Mines held an outreach programme in New Delhi on 13 October 2026 for prospective bidders and stakeholders.

international.headline: IMF’s October World Economic Outlook slightly raises 2026 global growth forecast
facts: The IMF released its October 2026 World Economic Outlook during the IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.
The IMF forecast global growth of 3.1% in 2026, up from its July forecast of 3.0%; it projected 3.4% growth in 2027.
The 2026 global forecast remains below the reported 3.5% expansion in 2025.
The IMF warned of risks linked to rising debt and the rapid expansion of artificial-intelligence investment.
No India or Andhra Pradesh growth estimate is included here because it was not independently verified from the available report material.
international.summary: The IMF published its October World Economic Outlook on 13 October in Bangkok, raising its global growth projection for 2026 slightly from the July estimate. The report also highlights debt and AI-related risks; its forecasts are projections, not observed outcomes.
international.staticLink: IMF surveillance; global economic outlook; business cycles and risks to growth.
international.prelimsTakeaway: WEO is the IMF’s assessment of global and member-country economic prospects; the October 2026 edition projects 3.1% global growth in 2026.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how geopolitical and energy shocks, public debt and technology-led investment can affect global growth and economic resilience.

international.headline: IMF’s Global Financial Stability Report warns that resilience does not mean risks have subsided
facts: The IMF published its October 2026 Global Financial Stability Report in Bangkok during the IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings.
The report describes global financial markets as resilient while judging financial-stability risks to remain elevated.
The IMF identifies possible AI-related market correction, risks in private credit, and leveraged or crowded hedge-fund positions as potential sources of stress.
The report calls for stronger financial-system resilience, close monitoring of banks and non-bank financial institutions, sustainable public debt and greater cyber resilience.
international.summary: The IMF released its Global Financial Stability Report on 13 October. Its central warning is that recent market resilience is not equivalent to safety, as financial vulnerabilities and potential stress channels remain elevated.
international.staticLink: Global financial stability; systemic risk; banking and non-bank financial institutions; financial regulation.
international.prelimsTakeaway: GFSR is an IMF assessment of global financial stability risks; the October 2026 report highlights AI-related repricing, private credit and leveraged hedge funds.
international.mainsAngle: Examine how leverage, interconnected financial institutions, technology-sector valuations and sovereign borrowing can transmit shocks across the global financial system.

international.headline: Shubman Gill named ICC Men’s Player of the Month for September 2026
facts: The International Cricket Council named India batter Shubman Gill its Men’s Player of the Month for September 2026 on 13 October.
Gill scored 333 runs in India’s first two September ODIs against the West Indies, including an unbeaten 223 in Guwahati.
India won the three-match ODI series 2–1; the ICC says this is Gill’s fifth monthly award and extends his record for most wins in the men’s award.
The ICC says Gill’s 223 was the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase; he reached his double-century in 117 balls, then the fastest in ODI history, according to the ICC.
international.summary: The ICC announced Gill as its September men’s monthly award winner on 13 October, recognising his ODI performances against the West Indies. The award followed a 333-run start to the series, including his unbeaten double-century in Guwahati.

international.headline: International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction 2026 focuses on resilience at home
facts: The International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction is observed annually on 13 October, as designated by the United Nations General Assembly.
The 2026 theme selected by the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction is “Resilience Starts at Home.”
The campaign emphasises risk-informed housing, household preparedness, inclusive early-warning communication and local planning.
The theme aligns with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030 and Sustainable Development Goal 11.
international.summary: Observed on 13 October, the 2026 international day places homes and household preparedness at the centre of disaster-risk reduction. UNDRR calls for risk-informed housing, accessible warning systems and stronger community resilience, with attention to unequal vulnerabilities.
international.staticLink: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction; disaster preparedness; resilient cities and communities.

international.mainsAngle: Discuss how resilient housing, accessible early warnings and inclusive local governance can reduce disaster losses, especially for vulnerable groups.
